the statement attributes an ongoing policy and implementation to Sisi.","ruler_attribution":"The parliamentary statement explicitly attributes continuing directives and removal campaigns to President el-Sisi.","limitations":["The source is a parliamentary statement and does not provide quantitative results, independent verification, or details of enforcement consistency."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9bd1344e8af7be93","start_unit":1,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The World Bank’s FY2023–2027 Country Partnership Framework with Egypt supported transforming the growth model toward greater inclusion and sustainability through private investment, human development, and resilience.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The framework was launched in 2023 and covers FY2023–2027; Ethiopia stated it would avoid significant harm during the 2023–2024 filling period.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","2B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The communiqué records a concrete diplomatic decision made on 13 July 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The Egyptian Presidency states that Sisi received Abiy Ahmed and that the two leaders reached the commitments.","limitations":["The source records the agreement and Ethiopian commitment but does not establish whether the four-month target or negotiated settlement was achieved."]},{"source_id":"SRC-24ac4884d856519b","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"In October 2023, four nuclear reactors were under construction at Egypt’s El Dabaa plant, as reported in an article describing African nuclear deployment; the article characterized the broader cooperation as civilian nuclear-energy capacity building, information sharing, networking, and training.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.4","1B.7","8B.6"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The reactor-construction status and cooperation report are dated 12 October 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source identifies Egypt’s El Dabaa project but does not establish Sisi’s specific decisions, safeguards, or oversight.","limitations":["The article provides no evidence about Egypt’s command-and-control, inspection, safety enforcement, nonproliferation compliance, or presidential attribution."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f36a1db5ec240098","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International’s retrospective account states that activist Alaa Abdel Fattah was arrested on 29 September 2019 amid a crackdown, sentenced in December 2021 by an Emergency State Security Court for an alleged false-news offense, and remained arbitrarily detained during 2023 despite the case’s relevance to his continued imprisonment.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source was published in 2025 but describes detention and legal circumstances continuing through the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The account concerns Egyptian authorities under Sisi but does not provide evidence of Sisi’s personal role in the arrest, conviction, or detention decisions.","limitations":["The source is retrospective and advocacy-oriented; the supplied text does not provide an independent judicial determination of every asserted violation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8a23eeab4e5bc7c6","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"On 24 September 2023, Egypt’s Water and Irrigation Ministry reported that the latest Egypt–Sudan–Ethiopia dam-talks round made no worthwhile progress, alleging that Ethiopia had reversed earlier accommodations and rejected proposed compromises;
